title: Super Defense
observed_goal: In the page-menu screenshot, the page text describes the goal as defending a campus and keeping the power core safe from drones; this goal was not converted into active gameplay execution or an observable cycle. The official card also claims team-building with student heroes and survival through escalating waves, but it was not playtested.
observed_controls: The screenshot shows buttons labeled Start your shift, Local high scores, Settings, How to play, and Open Source Licenses, plus a Hard Mode/Normal option.
The Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight keys and holding ArrowRight + Space for 900ms were tried in the capture, but their acceptance or gameplay effect was not observed.
No effective control for active gameplay was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
observed_core_loop: The core loop was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; no frame showing active gameplay, a wave, deployment, attack, defense, progress, or cycle repetition was recorded.
progress_feedback: Progress feedback during gameplay was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. The menu text only refers to Hard Mode with late drones +50% HP and faster, bigger waves; this is page text, not the result of gameplay execution.
decisions_risk_reward: Decisions, risk/reward, and the effect of selecting Hard Mode during gameplay were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. The presence of options in the menu alone does not prove game behavior.
rewards: Rewards, scoring, high score, or resources during gameplay were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; only the Local high scores button is visible in the menu.
penalties_failure: Failure, damage, resource loss, or penalties were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. No direct win/loss outcome was recorded.
outcomes_replay: An outcome, win, loss, wave ending, or replay capability was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
onboarding: The page presents a start menu with a title, textual description, Normal/Hard Mode selection, and a Start your shift button; successful entry into the game and interactive tutorial were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
visual_audio_accessibility: The screenshot shows a legible menu with a dark panel, text buttons, a colorful background image, and Settings and How to play options. Audio is not observable in a screenshot. Accessibility details, actual contrast, keyboard focus, and usable settings were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: The Technical trace indicates that the page was loaded with Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official and WebGL 2.0/Compatibility; this technical clue identifies the engine and does not establish game logic or controls.

The Technical trace reports streaming 36 sheets and the music files bgm_tension.ogg and bgm_boss.ogg becoming ready; the presence or readiness of a resource/asset does not establish that audio played or that a boss was reached.
The metadata value interaction_visual_change_signal is false and all five screenshots have the same sha256; this capture does not support accepted input or gameplay execution.
Software WebGL fallback warnings and 403/400 and remote-config errors appear in the trace; their effect on the game experience was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
transferable_principles: Before inferring a game loop, frames showing active state, an input-attributable change, and a repeatable outcome should be recorded.
A difficulty level should be accompanied by observable feedback and a clear consequence, not merely an option in the start menu.
The start interface should present the goal and next action briefly and clearly, while keeping card claims separate from evidence of actual execution.
Engine tracking and resource loading are only architectural clues and do not replace observation of interaction, progress, or outcome.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, only the general principle of separating onboarding from the game loop is transferable; this capture confirms no movement pattern or timing that can be adapted.
Any score/rank in Candle Climber should reflect skill only, and no purchase or wallet should create an advantage.
A free brake, horizontal direction change, or branching path requiring a new control should not be proposed; each is merely a hypothesis requiring separate testing, not a conclusion from this game.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce or propose this game’s name, characters, illustrations, art direction, text, audio, brand, or assets.
Do not transfer the card’s claim about heroes, combos, waves, or bosses as confirmed mechanics.
Do not use identical frames or a possible time-based change to conclude that input was accepted.
Do not copy the page’s specific structure or content as a direct Candle Climber template.

evidence.claim: Across all five stages, the same menu is visible with the title Super Defense, goal text, Hard Mode/Normal option, and start and menu buttons; active gameplay or an observable state change is not visible.

The page text says that training drones have been released and that heroes should be deployed, walkways should be held, and the power core should remain active; this is page goal text, and its execution was not observed.

The official card claims team-building with student heroes, use of elemental powers, chaining combos, and survival through escalating waves and screen-filling bosses; this claim was not confirmed by gameplay.
The metadata states interaction_visual_change_signal=false, all frames have the same hash, and the caveat explicitly says that a screenshot change is not proof of input comprehension.
The trace reports execution of Godot Engine v4.7.2, WebGL 2.0, streaming image sheets, and two music files becoming ready; these are technical clues and do not establish a loop or outcome.

limitations: Only the metadata-and-capture-evidence file and five input frames from this game were reviewed; no web browsing or rerun was performed. All frames have the same hash and the menu remains in them. stage_text is empty, inputs were merely attempted, and there is no direct evidence of active gameplay, a loop, an outcome, audio, score, or failure. The absence of game elements in the opening frame alone does not establish their absence throughout the game.
